entry.title: Find the hole a bolt fits
entry.summary: Davies’s later nuts-and-bolts example begins with fitting bolts into holes of different sizes. Turning the matching nuts adds another movement, with adult supervision for small parts.
entry.cue: Your child wants to compare sizes, fit objects, or turn a nut while holding a bolt.
detail: Her example uses a wooden board with differently sized holes and a container of matching nuts and bolts. The child can begin by finding which bolt fits which hole.
As the turning becomes interesting, one hand can hold the bolt while the other turns the nut. Organizing the pieces by size is another possibility; matching every piece is not required.
